title: Taiwanese Now Think They Need NT$16 Million to Retire
summaryZh: 台灣中高齡估退休需1614萬元，創新高
summaryHi: ताइवान के 40–64 वर्ष के लोग मानते हैं कि रिटायरमेंट के लिए 1.614 करोड़ NT$ चाहिए।
summaryEs: Los taiwaneses de 40 a 64 años creen que necesitan NT$16,14 millones para jubilarse.
summaryJa: 台湾の40〜64歳、老後資金は1614万台湾元必要と推計。
summaryKo: 대만 40~64세, 노후 자금 1,614만 대만달러 필요하다고 추정.
summaryEn: Taiwanese aged 40–64 now estimate they need NT$16.14 million to retire.
paragraphs: Middle-aged Taiwanese believe the price of a comfortable retirement is rising. A new survey found that people aged 40 to 64 now estimate they will need NT$16.14 million (about US$490,900) to support themselves in old age, up from NT$15.61 million last year.

The figures appear in the 2027 Ageless Society White Paper, published on Tuesday by the DBS Foundation and CommonWealth Magazine. It is based on 1,406 valid responses as well as input from a range of experts.

Respondents said their main financial concerns were medical and long-term care costs, unexpected major expenses, and inflation eating away at their assets. Partly as a result, the proportion planning to prepare through investing climbed from 39.4% to 46.1%, with time deposits and exchange-traded funds gaining popularity.

Even so, 41.2% admitted they lacked confidence in their financial preparations. On health, the share who felt unsure about their condition in later life dropped from 36.5% to 30.7%, yet fewer people reported getting enough sleep, exercising regularly or eating a balanced diet.

Ng Sier Han, general manager of DBS Bank Taiwan, urged people to start early and take advantage of compound interest, even if they can only save small sums. In his view, growing old is not the real problem; failing to prepare is. A Ministry of Labor official said the findings could feed into labor policy discussions.
How much money do you need when you stop working? People in Taiwan think the answer is getting bigger. A new report says they need about NT$16.14 million. That is about US$490,000.
The report is called the 2027 Ageless Society White Paper. DBS Foundation and CommonWealth Magazine made it. They asked 1,406 people. All of them were between 40 and 64 years old.
Last year, people said they needed NT$15.61 million. This year, the number is higher. People worry about the cost of doctors and care. They also worry that prices keep going up.
More people now want to invest their money. The number went from 39.4% to 46.1%. But 41.2% of people do not feel ready.
A bank boss said people should start saving early. Even small amounts can grow over time.

那大約是49萬美元。
這份報告叫做《2027無齡社會白皮書》。
星展基金會和《天下雜誌》製作了這份報告。
他們詢問了1,406個人。
這些人都在40到64歲之間。
去年，大家說需要新台幣1,561萬元。
今年，這個數字更高了。
大家擔心看醫生和照顧的費用。
他們也擔心物價一直上漲。
現在有更多人想把錢拿去投資。
這個比例從39.4%上升到46.1%。
但是有41.2%的人覺得自己還沒準備好。
一位銀行主管說，大家應該早點開始存錢。
就算是小錢，隨著時間也能慢慢變多。

paragraphs: People in Taiwan believe they will need more money for retirement than before. According to a new survey, people aged 40 to 64 think they will need NT$16.14 million, or about US$490,000, for their later years. Last year, the figure was NT$15.61 million.

The results come from the 2027 Ageless Society White Paper, which was released on Tuesday by the DBS Foundation and CommonWealth Magazine. The survey collected 1,406 valid answers and also included opinions from experts.

The biggest money worries were the cost of medical treatment and long-term care, sudden large expenses, and rising prices that make savings worth less. Because of this, more people are planning to invest. The share who want to prepare through investments rose from 39.4% to 46.1%, and bank deposits and ETFs became more popular.
However, 41.2% of people still said they were not confident about their financial plans. Fewer people said they slept enough, exercised regularly and ate a balanced diet.

Ng Sier Han, the general manager of DBS Bank Taiwan, said people should start early and let compound interest help them, even with small amounts. A Ministry of Labor official said the report could help with discussions about labor policy.
sentZh: 台灣人認為退休需要的錢比以前更多。
根據一項新調查，40到64歲的人認為晚年需要新台幣1,614萬元，約49萬美元。
去年這個數字是新台幣1,561萬元。
這些結果來自星期二由星展基金會和《天下雜誌》發布的《2027無齡社會白皮書》。
這項調查收集了1,406份有效回答，也納入了專家的意見。
最大的金錢煩惱是醫療和長期照顧的費用、突然出現的大筆開銷，以及讓存款貶值的物價上漲。
因為這樣，有更多人打算投資。
想透過投資來準備的人比例從39.4%升到46.1%，銀行定存和ETF也變得更受歡迎。
不過，仍有41.2%的人說他們對自己的財務規劃沒有信心。
說自己睡眠充足、規律運動和飲食均衡的人也變少了。
台灣星展銀行總經理伍維漢說，大家應該早點開始，讓複利幫助自己，就算金額很小也一樣。
一位勞動部官員說，這份報告有助於勞動政策的討論。

paragraphs: Middle-aged Taiwanese believe the price of a comfortable retirement is rising. A new survey found that people aged 40 to 64 now estimate they will need NT$16.14 million (about US$490,900) to support themselves in old age, up from NT$15.61 million last year.

The figures appear in the 2027 Ageless Society White Paper, published on Tuesday by the DBS Foundation and CommonWealth Magazine. It is based on 1,406 valid responses as well as input from a range of experts.

Respondents said their main financial concerns were medical and long-term care costs, unexpected major expenses, and inflation eating away at their assets. Partly as a result, the proportion planning to prepare through investing climbed from 39.4% to 46.1%, with time deposits and exchange-traded funds gaining popularity.

Even so, 41.2% admitted they lacked confidence in their financial preparations. On health, the share who felt unsure about their condition in later life dropped from 36.5% to 30.7%, yet fewer people reported getting enough sleep, exercising regularly or eating a balanced diet.

Ng Sier Han, general manager of DBS Bank Taiwan, urged people to start early and take advantage of compound interest, even if they can only save small sums. In his view, growing old is not the real problem; failing to prepare is. A Ministry of Labor official said the findings could feed into labor policy discussions.
sentZh: 台灣中年人認為，舒適退休的代價正在上升。
一項新調查發現，40到64歲的人現在估計，老年要養活自己需要新台幣1,614萬元（約49萬900美元），高於去年的新台幣1,561萬元。
這些數字出現在星展基金會和《天下雜誌》於星期二發表的《2027無齡社會白皮書》中。
白皮書根據1,406份有效回覆，以及多位專家的意見。
受訪者表示，他們主要的財務擔憂是醫療與長照費用、意外的大筆支出，以及通膨侵蝕資產。
部分因為這個原因，打算透過投資來準備的比例從39.4%攀升到46.1%，定期存款和指數股票型基金也越來越受歡迎。
即使如此，仍有41.2%的人承認對自己的財務準備缺乏信心。
在健康方面，對晚年身體狀況感到沒把握的比例從36.5%降到30.7%，但表示睡眠充足、規律運動或飲食均衡的人卻變少了。
台灣星展銀行總經理伍維漢呼籲大家及早開始、善用複利，即使只能存小額也一樣。
他認為，變老不是真正的問題，沒有做好準備才是。
一位勞動部官員表示，這些調查結果可以作為勞動政策討論的參考。

paragraphs: The sum Taiwanese believe they must amass before retiring continues to climb. According to a newly released white paper, people aged between 40 and 64 now reckon they will need NT$16.14 million, roughly US$490,900, to see them through their later years, compared with NT$15.61 million a year earlier.

The 2027 Ageless Society White Paper, jointly produced by the DBS Foundation and CommonWealth Magazine and unveiled on Tuesday, draws on 1,406 valid survey responses supplemented by expert commentary.

Healthcare and long-term care expenses topped the list of financial anxieties, followed by unforeseen large outlays and the erosion of savings by inflation. These fears appear to be nudging people towards markets: the proportion intending to fund their retirement through investment rose sharply, from 39.4% to 46.1%, while time deposits and exchange-traded funds attracted growing interest.

Confidence, however, remains fragile, with 41.2% saying they doubt their finances are in order. Respondents were somewhat less pessimistic about their health in old age, as the share lacking confidence fell from 36.5% to 30.7%, although fewer reported adequate sleep, regular exercise or a balanced diet.

Ng Sier Han, general manager of DBS Bank Taiwan, stressed the value of starting early and harnessing compound interest, however modest the amounts involved, arguing that ageing itself is less of a threat than inadequate preparation. A senior Ministry of Labor official added that the findings could inform future policy debates.
sentZh: 台灣人認為退休前必須累積的金額持續攀升。
根據一份新發布的白皮書，40到64歲的人現在估計，要撐過晚年需要新台幣1,614萬元，約49萬900美元，一年前則是新台幣1,561萬元。
由星展基金會與《天下雜誌》共同製作、於星期二公布的《2027無齡社會白皮書》，以1,406份有效問卷為基礎，並輔以專家評論。
醫療與長照支出高居財務焦慮之首，其次是無法預料的大筆開銷，以及通膨對存款的侵蝕。
這些擔憂似乎正把人們推向市場：打算靠投資支應退休生活的比例大幅上升，從39.4%增至46.1%，定存與指數股票型基金也吸引越來越多關注。
然而信心仍然脆弱，有41.2%的人表示懷疑自己的財務是否穩妥。
受訪者對老年健康稍微沒那麼悲觀，缺乏信心的比例從36.5%降至30.7%，不過表示睡眠充足、規律運動或飲食均衡的人變少了。
台灣星展銀行總經理伍維漢強調及早開始、善用複利的價值，無論金額多麼微小，他認為老化本身的威脅不如準備不足來得大。
一位勞動部高階官員補充說，這些結果可以為未來的政策辯論提供參考。

paragraphs: As life expectancy lengthens and living costs rise, the financial bar for a secure retirement in Taiwan is being raised accordingly. A white paper published on Tuesday indicates that citizens aged 40 to 64 now estimate they will require NT$16.14 million, approximately US$490,900, to sustain themselves after leaving the workforce, an increase from the NT$15.61 million cited in 2025.

Compiled by the DBS Foundation in partnership with CommonWealth Magazine, the 2027 Ageless Society White Paper is grounded in 1,406 valid questionnaire responses, complemented by the perspectives of specialists in the field.

The survey identifies medical and long-term care expenditure as the foremost source of financial apprehension, ahead of unanticipated major costs and the gradual depreciation of assets through inflation. Consequently, there has been a notable shift in strategy: the proportion of respondents who intend to rely on investment climbed from 39.4% to 46.1%, with fixed-term deposits and exchange-traded funds becoming increasingly favoured.

Nevertheless, a substantial minority of 41.2% conceded that they lacked confidence in their financial readiness. Attitudes towards health were mixed: while the share pessimistic about their physical condition in later life declined from 36.5% to 30.7%, fewer respondents reported maintaining sufficient sleep, regular exercise or a balanced diet.

Ng Sier Han, general manager of DBS Bank Taiwan, advocated beginning early and exploiting the power of compound interest, regardless of how modest one's contributions may be, contending that inadequate preparation rather than ageing per se constitutes the genuine risk. A senior Ministry of Labor official remarked that the report could usefully inform deliberations on labour policy.
sentZh: 隨著平均壽命延長、生活成本上升，台灣安穩退休的財務門檻也隨之提高。
星期二發表的一份白皮書顯示，40到64歲的民眾現在估計，離開職場後要維持生活需要新台幣1,614萬元，約49萬900美元，高於2025年提到的新台幣1,561萬元。
《2027無齡社會白皮書》由星展基金會與《天下雜誌》合作編製，以1,406份有效問卷為基礎，並輔以該領域專家的觀點。
調查指出，醫療與長照支出是財務憂慮的首要來源，排在意外大筆花費以及通膨導致資產逐漸貶值之前。
因此，理財策略出現明顯轉變：打算依靠投資的受訪者比例從39.4%攀升到46.1%，定期存款和指數股票型基金也越來越受青睞。
儘管如此，仍有41.2%這個不小的少數承認，對自己的財務準備缺乏信心。
對健康的態度則好壞參半：雖然對晚年身體狀況感到悲觀的比例從36.5%降到30.7%，但表示能維持充足睡眠、規律運動或均衡飲食的受訪者變少了。
台灣星展銀行總經理伍維漢主張及早開始，善用複利的力量，不論投入的金額多麼有限，他認為真正的風險在於準備不足，而不是老化本身。
一位勞動部高階官員表示，這份報告可以為勞動政策的審議提供有用的參考。
